# The archsimd feature check must dominate the vector block through
# a conditional branch: the AVX2 call, the test of its result, and
# the jump to the scalar block appear in that order, the instruction
# after the jump is the vector prologue (so the jump targets the
# scalar loop), and the masked tail load of the vector block follows.
# Sums stay correct with the check forced false (scalar path) and at
# v3 (check omitted).
[!GOARCH:amd64] skip 'gate branch objdump needs amd64'
[!GOOS:linux] skip 'host cpu probe reads /proc/cpuinfo'

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local
env GOEXPERIMENT=simd
env GOAMD64=v1
cd m

logos build -o $WORK/exe .
go tool objdump -s '^main\.sumI32$' $WORK/exe
stdout '(?s)CALL simd/archsimd\.X86Features\.AVX2\(SB\).*TESTL AL, AL.*JE'
# The instruction after the feature-false jump is the vector prologue:
# the jump targets the scalar loop. Swapped targets keep JE and
# VPMASKMOVD but put scalar code here.
stdout '(?s)CALL simd/archsimd\.X86Features\.AVX2\(SB\)[^\n]*\n[^\n]*TESTL AL, AL[ \t]*\n[^\n]*JE 0x[0-9a-f]+[ \t]*\n[^\n]*VPXOR'
stdout 'VPMASKMOVD'

env GODEBUG=cpu.avx2=off
logos run .
# The program observes the check itself: false here proves the sums
# below ran through the scalar loop the jump above targets.
stdout '^avx2 false$'
stdout '^sums ok$'

env GODEBUG=
env GOAMD64=v3
logos build -o $WORK/exe3 .
env GOAMD64=v1
exec go run ./runmin v3 $WORK/exe3
stdout '^(sums ok|host below v3)$'

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/gatebranch

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"simd/archsimd"
)

//go:noinline
func sumI32(xs []int32) int32 { return xs.sum() }

func oracleI32(xs []int32) int32 {
	t := int32(0)
	for _, v := range xs {
		t += v
	}
	return t
}

func main() {
	fmt.Println("avx2", archsimd.X86.AVX2())
	xs := make([]int32, 70)
	for i := range xs {
		xs[i] = int32(i*7 - 100)
	}
	if sumI32(xs) != oracleI32(xs) {
		panic("int32 sum mismatch")
	}
	fmt.Println("sums ok")
}

-- m/runmin/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
)

// runmin execs the binary named by its second argument only when the
// host CPU meets the GOAMD64 level given as the first argument (v1
// through v4); otherwise it prints "host below <level>" and exits 0.
// The cpuinfo probe is Linux-only: the script header skips elsewhere.
var levelFlags = map[byte][]string{
	'2': {"cx16", "lahf_lm", "popcnt", "sse3", "sse4_1", "sse4_2", "ssse3"},
	'3': {"avx", "avx2", "bmi1", "bmi2", "f16c", "fma", "lzcnt", "movbe", "osxsave"},
	'4': {"avx512f", "avx512bw", "avx512cd", "avx512dq", "avx512vl"},
}

// /proc/cpuinfo spells some feature names differently from the
// GOAMD64 docs: SSE3 reports as pni, LZCNT as abm, and OSXSAVE as
// xsave. Each entry lists every accepted spelling.
var flagNames = map[string][]string{
	"sse3":    {"sse3", "pni"},
	"lzcnt":   {"lzcnt", "abm"},
	"osxsave": {"osxsave", "xsave"},
}

func hasFlag(set map[string]bool, f string) bool {
	for _, name := range flagNames[f] {
		if set[name] {
			return true
		}
	}
	return set[f]
}

func main() {
	if len(os.Args) != 3 || len(os.Args[1]) != 2 || os.Args[1][0] != 'v' {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "usage: runmin v<level> <binary>")
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	data, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/cpuinfo")
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "read cpuinfo:", err)
		os.Exit(2)
	}
	set := map[string]bool{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(string(data), "\n") {
		if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "flags") {
			continue
		}
		parts := strings.SplitN(line, ":", 2)
		if len(parts) != 2 {
			continue
		}
		for _, f := range strings.Fields(parts[1]) {
			set[f] = true
		}
		break
	}
	for lvl := byte('2'); lvl <= os.Args[1][1]; lvl++ {
		for _, f := range levelFlags[lvl] {
			if !hasFlag(set, f) {
				fmt.Println("host below " + os.Args[1])
				return
			}
		}
	}
	cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[2])
	cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
	cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "runmin:", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
